خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ , [in the Kur lxiii. 4, meaning Pieces of wood made to lean, or incline, against a wall, (Jel,)] the latter word is with teshdeed because of its relation to many objects (لِلْكَثْرَةِ). (S.) ＝
-A2- مُسَنَّدَةٌ also signifies A certain sort of cloths, or garments; and so ↓ مَسْنَدِيَّةٌ . (M, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
